references.title: ChartKit llms.txt
references.note: Full file. This length is the cap. The other libraries are cut to this many bytes.
references.noDocsHint: Return one JSON object. version is "1". type is the chart name. data is the rows, or a number array when the chart is a single series. a11y.alt is one sentence. encoding.x is the category or date field and encoding.y is the measure. The renderer draws that object.

references.title: Recharts getting started and quickstart
references.note: Recharts publishes an llms.txt index of links, not a spec. This excerpt is the official getting-started page plus the start of quickstart, cut to the ChartKit cap. The Mintlify index blurb at the top of each page was removed.
references.noDocsHint: render() runs in a browser. renderToStaticMarkup returns an empty recharts-wrapper in Recharts 3.10.1 and draws nothing. Mount with react-dom/client createRoot and react-dom flushSync. Use a fixed width and height; ResponsiveContainer stays 0px. Put rows on data and field names on dataKey, and return the mounted markup.

references.title: Apache ECharts handbook: Get Started and Import
references.note: ECharts publishes an llms.txt index. The handbook link on that index is Get Started. This excerpt is that page plus Import ECharts, cut to the ChartKit cap. Apache License 2.0.
references.noDocsHint: In Node, call echarts.init(null, null, { renderer: "svg", ssr: true, width, height }) and return chart.renderToSVGString(). The SVG has to include the series marks. Put the numbers in series.data. Code that touches document or window runs in a browser instead.

references.title: Chart.js getting started: installation and usage
references.note: Chart.js does not publish an llms.txt. This excerpt is the official installation page plus the start of the usage guide, from the Chart.js docs (MIT), cut to the ChartKit cap.
references.noDocsHint: render() runs in a browser document. Create a canvas, register every scale and controller you construct, and leave that canvas in the document. A canvas tag or a data URL with no painted pixels does not pass. Put the numbers in the dataset data.

capability.reason: Recharts is a charting library for data visualizations like line charts, bar charts, etc. It does not support KPI cards or single-value metric displays.
ECharts does not have a built-in KPI card component. KPI cards are typically simple HTML/CSS layouts showing a single metric with delta, which is outside ECharts' chart rendering capabilities.
Chart.js does not support KPI card visualizations. It is designed for charts like bar, line, pie, etc., not single-value metric displays.
